subject: NUMVAL function
notes: CONFORMS SUSTAINED -- and, unlike the adjudication, it now survives the boundaries it had merely asserted. The general format has no optional or repeated element: FUNCTION and NUMVAL are both underlined (required) and there is exactly one parenthesized argument; the catalog row declares `IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1` and BindIntrinsicCore enforces it with COBOL1504 in BOTH directions. Three additional attacks were run and all failed to overturn it. (i) PB7's pattern -- a form that compiles and dies at run time: the FUNCTION-keyword-omitted form under `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` compiles AND RUNS correctly, so the omission license does not strand NUMVAL. (ii) Over-reservation: an intrinsic-function-name is not a reserved word unless the REPOSITORY declares it, and `01 NUMVAL PIC X(6)` is accepted alongside `FUNCTION NUMVAL(NUMVAL)` -- the lexer token does not leak into the user-defined-word space, so no legal source is rejected. (iii) The format has no reference-modification slot and NUMVAL is a numeric function; `FUNCTION NUMVAL("123.45")(1:2)` is rejected with COBOL1629 citing §8.4.3.3.3 SR2. test-ref left EMPTY deliberately: no spec-derived test pins the arity diagnostic or the general format, and CONFORMS-but-untested is the honest state. EDITIONS EMPTY: see AR-15.67.3-3's note -- the adjudication's '2014, 2023' was inferred from an Annex E absence and implies a false unavailability before 2014; IntrinsicCatalog's own `85` may not be used as the source. EVIDENCE: Probe pbnv09.cob: `FUNCTION NUMVAL(A1, A1)` -> `error COBOL1504: FUNCTION NUMVAL takes 1 argument(s); 2 given (ISO §15.3)`. Probe pbnv17.cob: `FUNCTION NUMVAL` with no argument list -> the same COBOL1504 with '0 given'. Probe E:/Temp/rfnv/rfnv04.cob (RFNVW04, --std 2023) with `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.`: CTRL `FUNCTION NUMVAL("12.5")` = +12.500000 and OMIT `COMPUTE R = NUMVAL("34.25")` = 00000003425000{ (=+34.250000), then REACHED-END. Probe rfnv07.cob (RFNVW07): `01 NUMVAL PIC X(6) VALUE "123.45".` with `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION NUMVAL(NUMVAL).` compiles and prints USERNAME=00000012345000{ (=+123.450000). Probe rfnv10.cob (RFNVW10): `MOVE FUNCTION NUMVAL("123.45")(1:2) TO T` -> `error COBOL1629: 'FUNCTION NUMVAL' is not an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function, so its result cannot be reference-modified (ISO 8.4.3.3.3 SR2).` Read: IntrinsicCatalog.cs `Add(new("NUMVAL", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "s", "Numval", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 85)); // §15.67`.
